steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The 6 Rs: Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Repair — a hierarchy for sustainable design decisions, from most to least effective.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Circular economy: products designed for disassembly, material recovery and reuse — eliminates waste, contrasts with linear 'take-make-dispose' model.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Life Cycle Analysis (LCA): assesses environmental impact from raw material extraction through manufacture, use and disposal — cradle-to-grave.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Planned obsolescence: designing products with limited useful life to drive repeat purchases — ethical concern, contributes to e-waste and resource depletion.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between a linear economy and a circular economy, using a smartphone as an example. | Describe how a designer could apply the 6 Rs to the development of a new office chair. | Discuss the ethical issues surrounding planned obsolescence in consumer electronics.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always define sustainability before applying it — 'meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs' Use specific product examples rather than abstract principles The 6 Rs are a hierarchy — Rethink is more effective than Recycle
